title: Reversing a longer list
description: Repeated reverse rewrites expose how the list changes step by step.
source:
theorem list_demo : [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].reverse = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1] := by
  rw [List.reverse_cons]
  rw [List.reverse_cons]
  rw [List.reverse_cons]
  rw [List.reverse_cons]
  rw [List.reverse_cons]
  rfl

steps.explanation: The initial goal is to show that reversing the list [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] produces [5, 4, 3, 2, 1].
Rewriting reverse_cons removes the head 1 from the list being reversed and appends it to the end.
The reverse operation now applies to [2, 3, 4, 5], while 1 remains at the end of the expression.
The reverse operation now applies to [3, 4, 5], with 2, then 1 appended after it.
The reverse operation now applies to [4, 5], with 3, 2, and 1 already appended.
The reverse operation now applies to [5], with 4, 3, 2, and 1 appended in that order.
The reverse of the empty list simplifies to the empty list, and reflexivity closes the equality.
